      <description><ul><li><p>41-year-old set on ‘dream to be able to race in Africa’</p></li><li><p>Rwanda to host despite criticism of human rights record</p></li></ul><p>Lewis Hamilton has said he hopes to remain racing in Formula One until he can take part in the African Grand Prix which is <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/oct/13/f1-returns-to-africa-for-first-time-since-1993-with-10-year-rwanda-deal-from-early-2030s">set to take place in Rwanda in the 2030s</a>. The seven-time world champion believes it is right that F1 is to hold a race there despite criticism of the country’s human rights record.</p><p>Last week F1 confirmed Rwanda was to host the African Grand Prix having concluded a 10-year agreement for the meeting on a purpose-built circuit, with the first race set for the early 2030s. It is lined up to be held on a circuit in Bugesera, 25 miles south of the capital, Kigali, which has yet to be constructed and marks a return to the African continent for the first time since it last held a race at Kyalami, South Africa in 1993.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/oct/22/lewis-hamilton-aims-to-extend-career-till-early-2030s-so-he-can-race-in-african-grand-prix">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Brazil keeps left: what Lula’s victory means for his country and beyond</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/26/brazil-presidential-elections-luiz-inacio-lula-da-silva-flavio-bolsonaro</link>
      <description><p>In today’s newsletter: As Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva secured victory in the presidential race, we look the implications for democracy, the environment and international relations</p><p>Good morning. Chances are you woke this morning to news of two momentous election results. In Serbia, a student-led movement has ousted the country’s long-serving leader, Aleksandar Vučić (which you can read more about <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/25/serbian-leader-aleksandar-vucic-concedes-defeat-in-fiercely-contested-parliamentary-election">here</a>). And just hours ago, Brazil’s president staged a <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/26/lula-wins-brazil-election">sensational turnaround</a> against his far-right opponent after a nail-biting vote.</p><p>Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, known as Lula, won a forth nonconsecutive term as president, seeing off far-right senator Flávio Bolsonaro, who spearheaded the radical populist movement built by his father and former president, Jair. Jair Bolsonaro is serving a 27-year prison sentence for plotting a coup after he lost the 2022 election.</p><p><em><strong>UK news </strong></em>| Two people have been killed and more than 160,000 properties have been left without power as <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026/oct/25/storm-boelo-warnings-scotland-northern-ireland-north-of-england-high-winds-uk">Storm Boelo continues to batter </a>the UK.</p><p><em><strong>Crime </strong></em>| British police are recording a <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026/oct/25/cocaine-linked-crimes-on-the-rise-in-britain-as-consumption-surges">growing number of crimes</a> linked to cocaine, including assaults, domestic abuse and dangerous driving, as figures show consumption has surged across England.</p><p><em><strong>France </strong></em>| Hundreds of thousands marched in cities across France on Saturday in largely peaceful <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/24/hundreds-of-thousands-march-across-france-in-protests-over-schools-and-policing">protests to support schoolchildren’s
